I'm computing the bond vectors for the N-CA-CB-CG dihedral in this ASP residue, then setting up the cross products needed to find the dihedral angle between the two planes.

Working through the vector math, I get n1 and n2, giving a dot product that yields a cosine of 0.5, suggesting a 60° angle, though I still need to determine the correct sign using the proper convention.

To resolve the sign, I'll compute the angle using atan2 with the cross product of n1 and n2 dotted against the normalized b2 vector, working through each component of the cross product and then normalizing b2 by its magnitude.

The dot product comes out positive at about 5.97, giving a positive angle through atan2, which resolves to a dihedral of +60°, so this is the g+ configuration.
